international.headline: India hosts BIMSTEC working group on counter-terrorism and transnational crime
facts: India hosted the 11th BIMSTEC Joint Working Group on Counter Terrorism and Transnational Crime in New Delhi on September 28–29, 2026.
Suhel Ajaz Khan, Additional Secretary (Counter Terrorism) in the Ministry of External Affairs, chaired the meeting.
All seven BIMSTEC members participated: Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka and Thailand.
Discussions addressed traditional and emerging non-traditional security threats and regional cooperation against terrorism and transnational organised crime.
international.summary: The meeting focused on regional coordination against security threats and transnational crime.
international.staticLink: JWG-CTTC stands for Joint Working Group on Counter Terrorism and Transnational Crime.
international.prelimsTakeaway: The 11th BIMSTEC JWG-CTTC meeting was hosted by India in New Delhi on September 28–29, 2026.
international.mainsAngle: Discuss the importance of regional cooperation in addressing cross-border security threats and transnational crime.

international.headline: 9th India–Kazakhstan joint military exercise KAZIND held in Oskemen
group2: Paper II: Indian Economy, AP Economy, Science & Technology
facts: The ninth KAZIND exercise was held in Oskemen, Kazakhstan, from September 28–October 11, 2026.

India fielded 60 personnel, primarily from a Garhwal Rifles battalion, alongside personnel from other arms and services and the Indian Air Force; Kazakhstan fielded an equal-sized contingent, mainly from its Land Forces.
The exercise aimed to improve interoperability and joint counter-terrorism capabilities in a sub-conventional environment under a United Nations mandate.
international.summary: The India–Kazakhstan exercise focused on counter-terrorism capabilities and joint operations.
international.staticLink: KAZIND is a bilateral exercise between India and Kazakhstan; its 2026 edition was the ninth.
international.prelimsTakeaway: The 2026 venue was Oskemen, Kazakhstan, and each side fielded 60 personnel.

national.headline: India discusses PRAHAAR, its national counter-terrorism strategy
facts: Union Home Minister Amit Shah unveiled the National Counter-Terrorism Policy and Strategy, PRAHAAR, on February 23, 2026; a conference discussing it was held in New Delhi on September 28, 2026.
The notes describe PRAHAAR as a 10-year institutional strategic framework under the Ministry of Home Affairs.

Its seven pillars are Prevention; Response; Aggregation of Internal Capabilities; Human Rights; Alleviating Conditions Conducive to Terrorism; Harmonising International Efforts; and Recovery & Resilience.
The stated full form is Policy for Response Against Hostile Activities and Radicalism.
national.summary: PRAHAAR sets out a multi-pillar national framework combining prevention, response, human rights, international cooperation and recovery.
national.prelimsTakeaway: PRAHAAR is the National Counter-Terrorism Policy and Strategy; its stated duration is 10 years and it has seven pillars.
national.mainsAngle: Examine how a comprehensive counter-terrorism framework can balance operational capacity, human rights, international cooperation and post-attack resilience.
